evidence: Ramamurthy was reacting to a case booked by the Jayanagar police against BJP booth-level agents for submitting Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of 5,698 voters during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The complaint was filed by former MLA Sowmya Reddy of Congress. ... “We [BJP] lodged a complaint with the [election] authorities on September 23 that there were 7,650 duplicate voters in Jayanagar that needed an inquiry,” ... The BJP leader said his party workers had moved the court seeking quashing of the FIR.
why: Verbatim, Deccan Herald (Bharath Joshi), 6 October 2026. Both sides are named office-holders and the claim attributes each to its party; no private person is named. FLAG, 5,698 against 2,245: the two counts are not the same thing and no source reconciles them. 5,698 is the number of voters the complaint says BJP agents' Form 7s sought to delete in one seat. 2,245 is the CEO's count of Form 7 applications received in the whole B.B.M.P (South) district from 16 June to 8 October 2026 (press note of 9 October, Annexure-3). The same press note encloses the CEO's letter of 1 October noting bulk Form 7 filings alleged to be not genuine. In Assam the CEO said bulk Form 7s found invalid were 'not counted as applications received' (lkp-07); no Karnataka source says the same, so it cannot be offered as the explanation. The site can state both figures, say what each counts, and say they are not reconciled. Jayanagar's 2023 margin was 16 votes (results_2023.csv).
